quizName: DMV Practice Test #15 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What color are warning signs, and what color is the lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT affect blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: How quickly the alcohol was consumed

questions.explanation: Three main factors affect BAC: the amount of alcohol consumed, how fast it was consumed, and body weight. Sex, physical condition, and food intake may also matter. How often someone drinks does not affect BAC.

questions.question: When following a car, where should you ride in the lane?
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of the lane. This way, the driver ahead will see you in their rearview mirror. Drivers check rearview mirrors more often than side mirrors.

questions.question: Why should you not change gears on railroad tracks?

options.text: Other drivers may not be expecting you to change gears.
The uneven surface may make it more difficult to switch gears.

questions.explanation: Do not shift gears when crossing railroad tracks. Your motorcycle could stall while on the tracks.

questions.question: What should you do to reduce your reaction time?

options.text: Ride slower than the speed limit.
Cover the clutch and the brakes.
Pull in the clutch when turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover the clutch and the brakes.
questions.explanation: Cover the clutch and brakes to reduce your reaction time. This is helpful when riding in areas where hazards may appear.

questions.question: What are the two most common types of motorcycle helmets?
questions.explanation: The two main helmet types are three-quarter and full-face. A full-face helmet provides the best protection.

questions.question: What gear should you be in when stopped?
questions.explanation: Shift down through the gears as you slow or stop. Stay in first gear when stopped so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: How often should you check your motorcycle's hydraulic fluid at minimum?
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before each ride to stay safe. Check hydraulic fluids and coolants at least once a week.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT affect blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: How fast the alcohol is consumed
How often the drinker consumes alcohol

questions.correctAnswerText: How often the drinker consumes alcohol
questions.explanation: Three main factors affect BAC: the amount of alcohol consumed, how fast it was consumed, and body weight. How often someone drinks does not affect BAC. Never drive after drinking alcohol.

questions.question: How do motorcycle headlights compare to car headlights?

options.text: Usually more powerful than a car's headlights.
Usually just as powerful as a car's headlights.
Usually not as powerful as a car's headlights.
Usually larger than a car's headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually not as powerful as a car's headlights.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle headlights are smaller and less powerful than car headlights.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are usually rectangular. They are white with black letters or symbols. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: Which of the following will help you ride safely on slippery surfaces?
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, slow down and use both brakes. Avoid sudden movements. Do not ride in the center of the lane. Follow the tire tracks left by cars. Watch for hazards like oil spots and loose gravel.

questions.question: Studies show that most crash-involved riders:

options.text: Under-brake the front tire and over-brake the rear tire.
Over-brake the front tire and under-brake the rear tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Under-brake the front tire and over-brake the rear tire.
questions.explanation: Most riders involved in crashes under-brake the front tire and over-brake the rear tire.

questions.question: A child passenger:

options.text: Should be placed in front of the operator.
Should be placed behind the operator.
Does not have to be able to reach the footrests.
Should hold onto the motorcycle frame.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be placed behind the operator.
questions.explanation: A child passenger should always sit directly behind the operator. A child in front may not balance well and could get in the way of the controls.

questions.question: If operating a three-wheeled motorcycle or riding with a sidecar, do not ride too far to the right of your lane because:

options.text: Other drivers may not see you.
You will not be able to pass other vehicles as easily.
Other drivers may try to share your lane.
You may run off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may run off the road.
questions.explanation: A sidecar extends to the right side of a motorcycle. Riding too far to the right risks the sidecar leaving the road. On a three-wheeled motorcycle, the rear right wheel may also leave the road if you get too close to the edge.

questions.question: Most motorcycles have rounded, or convex, mirrors. These mirrors:

options.text: Are easy to get used to right away.
Make cars seem closer than they actually are.
Provide a narrow view of the road.
Make cars seem farther away than they actually are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make cars seem farther away than they actually are.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors show a wider view than flat mirrors. They also make objects look farther away than they really are. Practice judging distances if you are not used to convex mirrors.

questions.question: If riding a three-wheel motorcycle in a group, you should travel in a:
questions.explanation: A staggered formation works well for two-wheeled motorcycles. Three-wheeled motorcycles are too wide for this formation. Ride in a single-file line instead.

questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes happen:

options.text: After riding for a long time.

questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on short trips. These trips are usually less than five miles long and at speeds slower than 30 miles per hour.

questions.question: When being passed from behind, you should:

options.text: Stay in the center portion of the lane.
Stay in the right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed from behind or by oncoming traffic, stay in the center of your lane. Moving closer to the passing vehicle puts you in danger.

questions.question: Which formation is best for a group of riders entering a curve?
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is usually best for groups to stay close while maintaining safe space. Use a single-file line when taking curves, turning, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: What happens when you brake while turning a curve?

options.text: It works the same as braking on a straight road.
You will have more grip as you lean into the curve.
You may have less grip as you lean into the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may have less grip as you lean into the curve.
questions.explanation: You can use both brakes while turning, but you must be very careful. When the motorcycle leans to turn, the tires use some of their grip for the turn. This leaves less grip available for braking.

questions.question: How should you choose your lane position?

options.text: Always ride in the center of the lane.
Always ride on the left side of the lane.
Always ride on the right side of the lane.
Change your position based on different conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your position based on different conditions.
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position. Choose where you are most likely to be seen and where you can keep space around you.

questions.question: Why should you not move to the far side of your lane when being passed?

options.text: It stops the other driver from returning to the lane too early.
It may cause the other driver to return to the lane too early.
It makes the other driver finish passing more quickly.
It makes other drivers want to pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It may cause the other driver to return to the lane too early.
questions.explanation: Moving to the far side of your lane when being passed is unsafe. It may make the other driver return to your lane before it is safe. Stay in the center of your lane when being passed.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, what should you NOT tell them to do?

options.text: Get on after the engine has started.
Sit as far forward as possible without crowding you.
Hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.explanation: Passengers should stay quiet and still so you can focus on riding. Passengers should only get on after the engine starts. They should sit forward without crowding you and hold on firmly to your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: What collects in the center of a traffic lane?

options.text: This is where motorcycle riders should always travel.
This is where most accidents happen.
This is where drivers least see motorcyclists.

questions.explanation: Trash and oil from cars collect in the center of a lane. Hazards like manhole covers can also be found there.
